# Release document fixtures

Private unit tests in `src/documents/tests.rs`, `src/policy/tests.rs`, `src/preflight/tests.rs` and `src/source/tests.rs` are registered by their modules; public process tests in `tests/commands.rs` exercise the closed dispatch, the fail-closed `preflight` and `audit-inputs` commands, and the closed POSIX bootstrap. Fixture documents, names and digests are fictional controls. Schema-valid fixtures demonstrate structural validation, not source approval, authenticated acquisition, complete SPDX coverage or release qualification.

The source-owned `../../schemas/spdx-2.3.schema.json` is retained byte-for-byte from the SPDX specification at commit `aadf3b0b8dbbabdb4d880b0fc714255fea436ff7`, path `schemas/spdx-schema.json`: 45,312 bytes, SHA-256 `239208b7ac287b3cf5d9a9af23f9d69863971102a5e1587a27a398b43490b89b`, JSON Schema Draft 7. SPDX specification contributors provide this material under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported; the original repository license is retained in `../../schemas/SPDX-LICENSE`. The schema has not been modified.

Source: [SPDX specification schema](https://github.com/spdx/spdx-spec/blob/aadf3b0b8dbbabdb4d880b0fc714255fea436ff7/schemas/spdx-schema.json), [upstream license](https://github.com/spdx/spdx-spec/blob/aadf3b0b8dbbabdb4d880b0fc714255fea436ff7/LICENSE).

The exact `jsonschema` 0.58.6 dependency is a locally tested evaluator candidate. Default HTTP, file, TLS and IDNA features and optional language bindings are disabled. Every evaluator construction selects a draft explicitly and uses `offline()` to reject unregistered references, including under feature unification. Production code selects only the three retained schemas; no schema-file CLI override exists. The synthetic prefix-items control qualifies Draft 2020-12 behavior alongside structural positive and negative tests of the governing index and qualification-result schemas.

Atomic-output callers must select a trusted parent directory. Source and process tests build their own Git repositories in temporary directories (`git init`, fictional files, fixed fictional author and committer dates) under a cleared environment; they never assert success against the developer checkout. Process fixtures copy the tracked cohort, tools and consumer policy bytes and may mutate only those copies, for example a candidate cohort listing its own `rc/` branch or structurally qualified tool pins with fictional digests. A clean fixture still fails at the closed qualified selector because pins are pending and authenticated acquisition receipts (Task 8) cannot be constructed; remote branch-tip ancestry and ruleset validation (Task 14) are not established locally. Producer execution and the POSIX bootstrap remain closed. Full real-artifact SPDX coverage remains Task 11 work.

The 640-byte `sha-mbles-1.bin` is the public SHA-1 chosen-prefix collision vector from the SHA-mbles research (Leurent and Peyrin, 2020), copied byte-for-byte from the `sha1-checked` 0.10.0 crate test data (SHA-256 `3ead211681cec93d265c8ac123dd062e105408cebf82fa6e2b126f4f40bcb88c`). The unit test hashes it directly to prove collision detection rejects it; Git-framed objects add a `<kind> <length>\0` header, so an attacker would have to include that header in the chosen prefix.

Fixture and process tests require a `git` executable on an absolute `PATH` entry; they build every repository under a cleared environment. Because preflight rejects any `.cargo/config` or `.cargo/config.toml` above the source root, the temporary directory used for fixtures must have no such ancestor layer; the fixtures assert this and name the offending file (set `TMPDIR` to a clean directory if needed).

The `index/candidate/` files are the golden output of the unqualified candidate release index assembly (`src/distribution.rs`), rendered from fictional entry facts in `src/distribution/tests.rs` and compared byte-for-byte by `distribution::tests::golden`. Every name, digest and commit is fictional except `policy_sha256`, which is the SHA-256 of the tracked `crates/trusted-server-cli/release-policy.json`, so the consumer accepts the producer policy as current; a change to that policy requires regenerating these files in the same change. The index bytes are named `candidate-release-index.json`, never `release-index.json`; the tag is the sentinel `v0.0.0-unqualified-candidate`; both signature bundle records per artifact are the empty-file record (size 0, SHA-256 of zero bytes) and no bundle file exists. The CLI's `release::evidence::candidate_fixture_tests` includes these files test-only (neither crate depends on the other), runs every unsigned consumer join over them and confirms that the consumer's non-empty bundle rule rejects the candidate. These fixtures grant no signing, publication or qualification authority.
